newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: MONGOLIA TRADE SURPLUS $12.5 MILLION IN JAN-JULY.
newsitem.headline: MONGOLIA TRADE SURPLUS $12.5 MILLION IN JAN-JULY.

text.p: Mongolia's trade surplus in the first seven months increased 10.6 percent to $12.5 million compared with $11.3 million in the same period last year, official statistics available on Tuesday showed.
That compared with a surplus of $19.6 million in the first half, the State Statistics Bulletin said.

Exports in the first seven months totalled $233.2 million compared with $257.3 million last year, while imports totalled $220.7 million against $246 million in the year-ago period, the figures showed.
In July alone, exports were $33.5 million, up from $33.4 million a year ago, while imports rose to $40.6 million from $33.3 million last year.
Of exports in the first seven months, $128 million was earned from mineral products and $55.9 million from garments. Mongolia's main export item is copper concentrate.
Imports of machinery, equipment and electric appliances reached $63.5 million while imports of mineral and petroleum products stood at $45 million.
Of exports, Mongolia earned $88.3 million from Switzerland, $53 million from China, and $20.9 million from Russia.
Mongolia imported goods worth $75.7 million from Russia, $30.8 million from China, and $23 million from Italy.
